title: Ops Sherpa: taskflow templates and admin shortcuts for runbook-driven support
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Support engineers and SREs currently follow ad-hoc runbooks stored in Confluence and a mix of ad-hoc Linear tickets. This ticket implements 'Ops Sherpa' — a lightweight taskflow layer that converts canonical runbooks into reusable task templates, plus a small admin utilities surface (CLI and Slack shortcuts) that lets on-call engineers instantiate, monitor, and escalate those taskflows safely. Goals: (1) reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) by removing manual checklist creation, (2) preserve auditable step execution for compliance, (3) make runbook updates propagate to new task instances without breaking in-flight incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Create taskflow template format and storage (YAML + metadata) and a generator that converts a template into a Linear task tree
Implement admin CLI with commands: ops-sherpa create|status|cancel|replay and Slack shortcuts to create a taskflow from a template
Taskflow instantiation records step-level metadata (actor, timestamps, artifacts links) in the Linear ticket and emits events to our observability pipeline
Safe defaults: instantiated taskflows run in 'manual-step' mode by default; any automatic steps require explicit opt-in and an ACL check
Alpha rollout executed with SRE and Support triage team (at least 10 incidents handled with Ops Sherpa) and MTTR baseline measured
Docs and runbook mapping docs published and a migration script to convert 20 high-volume runbooks into templates
tasks: Design taskflow schema and validation rules (YAML fields, step types, pre/post hooks)
Prototype generator that creates Linear subtasks from template steps
Build lightweight admin CLI (Go) using opsctl patterns and auth via internal SSO tokens
Slack interactivity: message action + workflow to kick off a template from Slack
Instrumentation: emit events to metrics/trace pipeline and add per-task tags for model/region/customer where applicable
Create migration utility to map existing Confluence runbooks to templates and flag ambiguous steps for manual review
Write docs: quickstart, template authoring guide, and postmortem checklist integration
Run alpha with SRE: collect feedback, iterate on step types and error modes
technical_notes: Architecture: templates stored in git under infra/ops-sherpa/templates. Generator reads a template, validates YAML, and calls Linear API to create a parent ticket + child tasks. Metadata blob is attached as a ticket comment for auditability.
Security: instantiation checks use RBAC from identity service. Opt-in automatic steps require a signed policy in the template and a KMS-backed approval token.

Tradeoffs: implementing a full stateful workflow engine (temporal/zeebe) would provide stronger guarantees but adds operational complexity. We prefer templated Linear tasks for early rollout to minimize infra burden and keep task visibility native to the engineering workflow.
Idempotency: each template includes 'idempotency_key' optional field. Generator will detect duplicate instantiations within a 24h window to avoid repeated work during noisy alerts.

Observability: each task creation emits a span with tags: template_id, incident_id, created_by. We'll add dashboard panels in Console: 'Ops Sherpa instantiations', 'Average manual steps per run', and 'MTTR for Sherpa-supported incidents'.

review_feedback: PM (Diego Ramos): prefer explicit 'escalate' step type that creates a high-priority child ticket and notifies PagerDuty
Design (Maya Ortiz): include a 'context' template field so runbook authors can include links to dashboards and log queries
SRE (Priya Nair): automatic remediation steps should be blocked in the first two sprints; focus on reliable telemetry first
Security (Jordan Blake): store template signatures and require signed template to enable 'auto' mode. Also ensure audit logs are forwarded to the central compliance bucket.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental automatic remediation causes customer impact. Mitigation: default to manual steps and require signed opt-in for auto-steps; add a kill-switch endpoint to cancel running automations.
Risk: duplicate task instantiations during noisy alerts. Mitigation: idempotency_key detection and a 24h de-dup window; user confirmation in Slack if duplicates are detected.
Risk: templates diverge from living runbooks. Mitigation: scheduled quarterly sweep and a template linter that runs on PRs to the templates directory.
Risk: visibility gap for compliance. Mitigation: attach full step execution JSON as an encrypted artifact to the Linear ticket and push audit records to the compliance S3 bucket.
Risk: scaling Slack interactions. Mitigation: implement per-workspace rate limits and backpressure responses; queue long-running template instantiations with status updates.
rollout_plan: Alpha (SRE + Support triage): 2 weeks. Objective: validate template types and CLI ergonomics. Success criteria: at least 10 incidents handled, no accidental auto-remediations.

Beta (wider Support + select Product teams): 4 weeks. Objective: evaluate user experience and measure MTTR delta. Success criteria: 20% reduction in task creation time and positive qualitative feedback.
GA: enable for all internal teams after policy and docs complete. Provide 'template authoring' office hours and a migration script for remaining runbooks.
migration_plan: Identify top 20 runbooks by pageview and incident frequency
Run migration script that converts sections into template steps and flags ambiguous steps for manual editing
Create a 'template-review' label and queue for PM/design review before merging templates
Deprecate old Confluence runbook pages in favor of canonical template repo after 90 days
